name: Jak and Daxter Trilogy (OpenGOAL)
post_apply_message:
Jak and Daxter Trilogy (OpenGOAL) — NATIVE LINUX, no Proton. Apply adds a Steam shortcut for the launcher AppImage with NO compat tool set, because this runs natively; forcing Proton on it would break it.

THE APPIMAGE PROBABLY NEEDS ITS EXECUTABLE BIT BACK. Files copied from the SMB share may land without +x depending on the mount's file_mode, and an AppImage that isn't executable simply won't start. Check and fix with:
    ls -l 'OpenGOAL-Launcher_2.10.4_amd64.AppImage'
    chmod +x 'OpenGOAL-Launcher_2.10.4_amd64.AppImage'
There is no recipe step for this yet — see the notes.

THE LAUNCHER WILL NEED A LINUX BUILD OF OPENGOAL. versions/official/v0.3.3/ contains gk.exe, goalc.exe and extractor.exe — WINDOWS binaries, which are no use here. On first run the launcher will want to download the Linux build for whichever version you pick. That needs the Deck online once.

THE ISOs ARE RIGHT THERE, WHICH IS THE POINT. All three sit at the top of the game folder, so when the launcher asks for a source you point it at the folder instead of hunting: Jak 1 (Precursor Legacy, EU), Jak II (USA v2.01) and Jak 3 (EU/AU). If the launcher decides to re-extract and recompile for Linux, it has everything it needs locally and never has to ask you for a disc image.

POINT THE LAUNCHER AT THE NEW PATH. OpenGOAL keeps its own config in ~/.config outside the game folder, so it does NOT travel with Deploy. After deploying you'll need to tell the launcher where the install folder now lives — once, on that machine.

SPACE: this is ~34 GB deployed. If the launcher rebuilds for Linux, active/*/out (12.9 GB, compiled by the Windows toolchain) and active/*/iso_data (9.65 GB, re-extractable from the ISOs beside them) become regenerated rather than reused — at which point roughly 22 GB of what was copied is redundant and can be trimmed. Worth checking what it actually reuses before deciding.
notes:
Built 2026-07-31. OpenGOAL (opengoal.dev) is a DECOMPILATION + reimplementation with its own launcher, not a static recompilation like the Skate 3 / N64Recomp entries — so it behaves differently: the launcher owns version management and install layout, and the 'game' is data compiled from the ISO rather than a shipped executable.

Staged to NAS _games/'Jak and Daxter Trilogy' at Tony's explicit request to include BOTH the launcher and the ISOs so the launcher never has to fish for a disc image. 34,078 files / 34.15 GB. Excluded only 'OpenGOAL Windows Launcher.msi' (wrong platform — he wants the native Linux AppImage).

CONTENT BREAKDOWN: ISOs 9.9 GB (Jak1 EU 1.39, Jak2 USA 4.21, Jak3 EU/AU 4.29), active/*/iso_data 9.65 GB, active/*/out 12.89 GB, decompiler_out 1.28 GB, goal_src 0.27 GB, versions/ 0.17 GB (WINDOWS exes only), launcher AppImage 0.13 GB.

NO PROTON DEPLIBERATELY: the steam_shortcut step omits 'proton' entirely, so no CompatToolMapping is written. steam_shortcut already skips the compat mapping on Windows hosts; here it's skipped because the target IS a native Linux binary.

NO make_executable STEP EXISTS. The AppImage needs +x and there's no step type for it, so it's documented in post_apply_message instead of automated. This will recur — Super Smash Bros 64 (Battleship) is also an AppImage, and more native-Linux recomps are likely. A small 'make_executable' step (chmod +x on a list of paths under game_dir) is the clean fix; proposed to Tony, not built, since it's a new step type rather than a bug fix.

EXE NAME CARRIES A VERSION (OpenGOAL-Launcher_2.10.4_amd64.AppImage), so a launcher update renames it and both marker_files and the shortcut exe go stale. Re-point them when the launcher is updated.

save_paths RESOLVED 2026-08-12 (they were left empty pending confirmation). PCGamingWiki's OpenGOAL page gives them, and note these are XDG paths, NOT the {appdata} template PCGW's Windows column implies: this runs as a NATIVE Linux AppImage with no Proton prefix, so {appdata} would resolve into a prefix that doesn't exist and the step would fail. One path per game — jak1/jak2/jak3 each keep their own saves/<uid>/ folder.

No existing Steam shortcut for it, so the appid derives from the recipe id — no registry pin needed. UNTESTED on hardware.

save_paths added 2026-08-12 from PCGamingWiki (Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy (OpenGOAL)) — Windows path translated to GFM's platform-aware templates. NOT verified against a live save folder; a capture that comes back empty means the path is wrong.
